content.text: Confirmed pass-through - the tainted request parameter name flows unchanged into the `File` constructor, which is a classic path traversal sink. This is the standard OWASP Benchmark true-positive pattern.

input.justification: The tainted data originates from request.getParameterNames()/getParameterValues (user-controlled HTTP parameter name), is passed to an inner class method Test.doSomething, which forwards it unchanged to ThingFactory.createThing().doSomething(param). The concrete implementation (Thing1/Thing2) is a pure pass-through (returns the input unmodified), so 'bar' retains the exact attacker-controlled value. This value is then used directly as a path segment in 'new java.io.File(new java.io.File(TESTFILES_DIR), bar)' with no sanitization, normalization, or validation of path traversal sequences (e.g., '../'). This matches the classic OWASP Benchmark path-injection true-positive test pattern.
